corner.line: And a crowd of young boys, they're fooling around in the corner
stanza: And a crowd of young boys, they're fooling around in the corner
Drunk n' dressed in their best brown baggies and their platform soles
They don't give a damn about any trumpet-playing-band
It ain't what they call "Rock n' Roll"

corner.line: I was standin' on a noisy corner
stanza: I slept last night in a good hotel
I went shoppin' today for jewels
The wind rushed around in the dirty town
And the children let out from their school
I was standin' on a noisy corner
Waitin' for the walkin' green
Across the street, he stood
And he played real good
On his clarinet for free

corner.line: I was standing on a noisy corner
stanza: I was standing on a noisy corner
Waiting for the walking green
Across the street he stood
And he played real good
On his clarinet for free

corner.line: I asked the boys on the corner
stanza: I asked the boys on the corner
Did they know how many them things you think is out on the road
The one I mean
I say if you seen her you know her
Pretty little thing riding by in a champagne Corolla

corner.line: Follow my shadow around your corner
stanza: Downtown hotspot halfway up the street
I used to be free, I used to be seventeen
Follow my shadow around your corner
I used to be seventeen, now you're just like me

corner.line: But you know I'd stand on the corner
stanza: You were screamin' at the Evangelicals
They were screamin' right back from what I remember
When you said, "I will never be your vegetable"
Because I think when you're gone, it's forever
But you know I'd stand on the corner
Embarrassed with a picket sign
If it meant I would see you when I die
Beneath the porch-light
We've all been circling
Beat our dust hearts;
Singe our flour wings
But in the corner
Something is happening!
Wild Cosmia, what have you seen?

corner.line: Of the café on the corner
stanza: He folds up his job form
Gets up from his chair
The next person sits down with a similar air
Of dejection
He walks out, heads in the direction
Of the café on the corner
For a coffee and some headroom

corner.lineNext: I'm nearly down on one knee

corner.line: I've got a coat and some friends on the corner
stanza: Mother, don't worry
I've got a coat and some friends on the corner
Mother, don't worry
She's got a garden we're planting together
Mother, remember the night
That the dog had her pups in the pantry?
Blood on the floor and fleas on their paws
And you cried till the morning
